newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan state asks for help to end famine - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan state asks for help to end famine - paper.

text.p: Sudan's northeastern Red Sea state has asked the central government and its neighbours to help end a famine that is threatening 240,000 people, a privately-owned newspaper reported on Sunday.
The Alwan daily said that according to a report by the state's emergency committee, there was widspread malnutrition among children, women and the elderly in five provinces.

Last week, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Cresent Societies (IFRC) in Nairobi said it was preparing an appeal to assist 158,000 of the 240,000 Beja people in the Red Sea Hills through rations of oil, pulses and cereals.
Two years of crop failure and little rainfall have hit the region hard. The IFRC said that the Beja relied on livestock for survival but grain costs had shot up while animal prices fell.
The Alwan reported that the emergency committee had proposed setting up food centres in hospitals to provide up to 60 percent of the area's needs.
